record.name: Evacuation
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Evacuation: extract map-placed Civilians or enemy HVTs using Extraction Consoles, with two Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, score 1 Objective Point for each of the four Civilians successfully Extracted using an Extraction Console (up to four).
At game end, score 1 Objective Point for each opposing HVT successfully Extracted using an Extraction Console (up to two).
Each player has two Classified Objectives, worth 2 Objective Points each when completed (up to four), as specified explicitly in the English publication.

rules.name: Forces and Deployment
paragraphs: Players deploy at opposite table edges. Both Deployment Zones are [[distance:8:inch]] deep in 150-point games and [[distance:12:inch]] deep in 200–400-point games. Both languages show these dimensions on their published maps.
Troopers cannot deploy in Silhouette contact with a Civilian. Civilians and Extraction Consoles occupy fixed positions on the mission map; HVTs follow their normal player-selected deployment rules.

rules.name: Civilians
paragraphs: Four Civilians begin at the positions indicated on each game-size map. Each must be on an accessible point of the table, not on top of or inside scenery or buildings; terrain placement must allow this.

Use suitable civilian/HVT Models or Player A/B Tokens as the source permits. ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 sets Player A/B Tokens at 25 mm, but does not prescribe Civilian Model base sizes; map symbols indicate center positions only.
Civilians may be CivEvaced under the applicable CivEvac rules. Extraction is a separate successful Scenario Skill, not automatic from being CivEvaced.

rules.name: Multiple HVTs
paragraphs: Each player deploys two HVTs under the normal HVT deployment rules. The opponent's HVTs are eligible for Extraction and score 1 Objective Point each when successfully Extracted.
HVT locations are not fixed by the printed map. The four printed blue markers represent Civilians, not player-deployed HVTs.

rules.name: Extraction Consoles
paragraphs: Two Extraction Consoles begin on the table centerline at the printed positions. Each is a Console A Token or scenery matching its 40 mm diameter (ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14).
The Consoles are shared extraction points; activating a Console does not itself award points or establish exclusive ownership.

rules.name: Activate Extraction Console

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Extraction Console and CivEvacing a Civilian or enemy HVT may declare this Skill.
effects: Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts may be repeated.
On success, select one currently CivEvaced Civilian or enemy HVT, mark it Extracted, and remove it from the table.
restrictions: The English source prohibits this Skill during the first Game Round.
clarifications: The Spanish text uses 'primer Turno de Juego' for the opening restriction and explicitly permits re-Activating a Console activated by the opponent; the English source is silent on that latter point.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Extraction Console and CivEvacing at least one Civilian or enemy HVT may declare this Skill.
The English publication prohibits this Skill in the first Game Round. The Spanish publication instead uses 'primer Turno de Juego'; the different timing term is retained as a source issue.

Spend a Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. If it fails, another attempt can be made by spending another Short Skill. On success, choose one of the Civilians or enemy HVTs currently CivEvaced by that Specialist Troop, mark it Extracted and remove it from the table.

The Spanish source expressly states that a Console may be Activated after the opponent has Activated it; the English text is silent. Extraction is per successful action, not permanent Console Control.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform mission tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: If a Specialist Troop fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, its next consecutive Order using the same Skill and target receives +3 to WIP. The third and subsequent consecutive Orders receive +3 and +1SD. These MODs are cumulative with other applicable Scenario MODs.

The sequence resets on a successful Roll, using a different Skill or target, an interruption, or an Order spent on another Trooper. Only one sequence per Trooper and Scenario-labelled Skill applies at once.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 55 explicitly gives 2 Objective Points per Classified Objective for two Objectives. ES p. 50 instead states two Classified Objectives and '2 Puntos de Objetivo' without 'each'. Preserve this language-scope ambiguity; follow the explicit English scoring.

ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 57 prohibits Activate Extraction Console in the first Game Round; ES p. 52 uses 'primer Turno de Juego' (first Game Turn), not the usual Spanish term for Game Round. Preserve the unresolved timing distinction.

ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 52 expressly allows reactivating a Console previously activated by an opponent; EN p. 57 does not contain the corresponding sentence. One successful activation extracts one CivEvaced subject.

record.name: Hardlock
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Hardlock: Activate three centerline Consoles, pick up and Control the opposing Beacon, and complete one Classified Objective.

condition.text: At the end of each Game Round, be the only player with a non-Null Trooper as a Model (not a Marker) in Silhouette contact with the Enemy Beacon; enemy Troopers in contact prevent Control.
At the end of the game, your own Beacon is not Controlled by the enemy.
Complete your single Classified Objective (1 Objective Point).

rules.name: Deployment and objective positions
paragraphs: Sides A and B deploy on opposite table edges in game-size-specific Deployment Zones. Troopers may not deploy in Silhouette contact with any Beacon or Console.

There are two Beacons, one for each player, positioned in the middle of the front edge of each Deployment Zone. The one beside the opponent's Deployment Zone is the Enemy Beacon. Three Consoles stand along the table centerline: one at the center, with the others [[distance:6:inch]] from the side edges at 150 points, [[distance:8:inch]] at 200/250 points and [[distance:12:inch]] at 300/350/400 points. Each Console uses a Console A Token or scenery of the same diameter as that Token; the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart gives Console Tokens 40 mm and Beacon Tokens 25 mm.

rules.name: Pick Up Beacon

requirements: The player must have an Activated Console.
The Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with either a friendly Trooper in Normal State carrying the Enemy Beacon, or an unaccompanied Enemy Beacon without an opposing non-Null Trooper in contact.
effects: Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Enemy Beacon without making a Roll. Follow the Common Rules of Beacons.
sourceNotes: The Spanish source calls the prerequisite a Connected Console rather than an Activated Console; the wording remains an unresolved source discrepancy.

paragraphs: Pick Up Beacon is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill, requiring that the player has an Activated Console. The Trooper must also be in Silhouette contact either with a friendly Trooper in Normal State carrying the Enemy Beacon, or with an unaccompanied Enemy Beacon with no opposing non-Null Trooper in contact.

Spend one Short Skill to pick up the Enemy Beacon without a Roll. Follow the Common Rules of Beacons. The Spanish source calls the prerequisite a Connected Console rather than an Activated Console; see the source issue below.

rules.name: Common Rules of Beacons
paragraphs: Each Model can carry one Beacon; a Trooper with the Baggage Special Skill can carry up to two. Only Models, not Markers (including Camouflaged, Impersonation or Holoecho Markers), may carry a Beacon.

Beacons remain on the table and in Silhouette contact with their carrier. When the carrier enters or is in a Null State, the Beacon is dropped slightly outside Silhouette contact. Beacons do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Control an Enemy Beacon
paragraphs: A player Controls an Enemy Beacon only while that player alone has at least one Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Opposing Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Activate Console

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate the Console. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
A player may Activate a Console already Activated by the opponent, removing the previous player's Activated status. Different Player Tokens can track the current player.

paragraphs: Activate Console is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console must succeed on a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts can be repeated, spending a Short Skill for each attempt.

A player may Activate a Console already Activated by the opponent, using the same procedure. The previous player's Activated status is removed. Different Player Tokens can indicate which player currently has each Console Activated.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops in Hardlock.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Classified Objective
paragraphs: Each player has one Classified Objective, worth 1 Objective Point if completed.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 60 requires an Activated Console to Pick Up Beacon, whereas ES p. 55 says 'Consola Conectada'; its activation procedure on ES pp. 56-57 uses both Conectada and Activada. Preserve the terminology discrepancy without asserting a second Console state.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 60 requires a friendly Beacon carrier in Normal State for transfer; ES p. 55 does not repeat the Normal State qualification. Preserve the English restriction and the bilingual gap.

record.name: Uplink Center
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Uplink Center: Activate and Control the two Communication Antennas, Control the Tech-Coffin and keep an Active Lieutenant.

condition.text: Have a [[skill:lieutenant|Lieutenant]] who is not in a Null, Isolated or Immobilized State at the end of the game.

rules.name: Deployment and objectives
paragraphs: Sides A and B deploy on opposite sides of the game table. Neither player may deploy in Silhouette contact with the Tech-Coffin or Communication Antennas.

Two Communication Antennas are on the table centerline, [[distance:6:inch]] from the side edges at 150 points, [[distance:8:inch]] at 200/250 points, and [[distance:12:inch]] at 300/350/400 points. The Tech-Coffin is at the table center. Each objective uses its named Token or scenery of the same diameter; the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart gives Transmission Antenna and Tech-Coffin Tokens 40 mm.

rules.name: Activate Communication Antenna

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Communication Antenna may declare this Skill.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate the Antenna. Failed attempts can be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
The opponent may Activate an already Activated Antenna. A successful new Activation removes the previous player's Activated status; track the current player with Player Tokens.

paragraphs: Activate Communication Antenna is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an Antenna makes a Normal WIP Roll to Activate it. Failed attempts may be repeated, spending a Short Skill each time.

The opponent can Activate an already Activated Antenna using the same procedure. When this succeeds, it stops counting as Activated for the previous player. Use Player Tokens to identify which player currently has each Antenna Activated.

rules.name: Control a Communication Antenna
paragraphs: A player Controls an Antenna at the end of the game when that player alone has at least one non-Null Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Enemy Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Control the Tech-Coffin
paragraphs: The Tech-Coffin is Controlled at the end of the game when a player alone has at least one non-Null Trooper as a Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact with it. Enemy Troopers in Silhouette contact prevent Control; Models in a Null State do not count.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: After failing a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, a Specialist Troop gains +3 on the next consecutive Order for the same Skill and target; the third and subsequent consecutive Orders gain +3 and +1SD. These MODs are cumulative with other applicable Scenario MODs.
The sequence resets after a successful Roll, a different Skill or target, or an Order spent on another Trooper. Only one active sequence per Trooper and Scenario-labelled Skill is permitted.

rules.name: Active Lieutenant
paragraphs: At the end of the game, a Lieutenant is Active only if they are not in a Null State (such as Unconscious, Dead or Sepsitorized), Isolated State or any Immobilized State.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: HVT Models are not deployed, Secure HVT does not apply, and players do not use the Classified Deck in this mission.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 94 explicitly groups 300/350/400-point games for the [[distance:12:inch]] Antenna offset, but ES p. 100 lists only 400/300. Both printed mission maps (EN p. 93, ES p. 99) group 300/350/400 in the same layout. Treat the Spanish sentence as an omission, not an alternate 350-point placement.

record.name: Battleground
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Battleground: dominate three Sectors for 1/3/4 Objective Points and Kill or alternatively Threaten the enemy Key Ops.

objectives.name: Enemy Key Ops: Kill or Threaten

condition.text: Kill the enemy Key Ops: it enters Dead State, is in a Null State at the end of the game, or has not been deployed on the table as a Model or Marker by game end.

Alternatively to Killing (not in addition), at the end of the game Threaten the enemy Key Ops with at least one friendly non-Null Trooper represented as a Model (not a Marker) inside its Zone of Control.

rules.name: Sectors (ZO)
paragraphs: Three Sectors are identified only when the game has finished, not before. Each is a Zone of Operations spanning the table width. The central Sector straddles the table centre; the other two are on opposite sides.

In 150-point games, each Sector is [[distance:4:inch]] deep, with the outer Sectors positioned [[distance:2:inch]] from the central line. In 200-400-point games, each Sector is [[distance:8:inch]] deep, with the outer Sectors positioned [[distance:4:inch]] from the central line.
The displayed map locates the end-of-game scoring areas for reference; it does not instruct players to mark the areas before the game ends.

rules.name: Dominate a Zone of Operations
paragraphs: A player Dominates a Sector when they have more Victory Points of eligible Troopers inside it than their opponent. Models, Trooper Markers, Proxies and [[skill:peripheral|Peripheral]] Troops count; Troopers in a Null [[trait:state|State]], equipment Tokens and fake Holoechoes do not.
More than half of a Trooper's base must lie inside the Sector for it to count toward Dominating that Zone of Operations.

rules.name: Embryo eligibility
paragraphs: Troopers possessing [[skill:shasvastii|Shasvastii]] count toward Domination while in [[state:unconscious|Unconscious]] or any non-Null [[trait:state|State]].

rules.name: Bonus for equipped Troopers
paragraphs: [[equipment:baggage|Baggage]] grants an additional 20 Victory Points toward Dominating the Sector when its Trooper is inside that Sector and is in a non-Null [[trait:state|State]].

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: Troopers count as Killed if they enter [[state:dead|Dead State]], are in a Null [[trait:state|State]] when the game ends, or were not deployed on the table as a Model or Marker by the end of the game.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model or use the Classified Deck. The Secure HVT rule does not apply.

rules.name: Key Ops
paragraphs: At the end of Deployment, in Initiative order, each player designates a Key Ops from their Army List. The chosen Trooper must be deployed on the table as a Model, not a Marker or in Hidden Deployment, and must remain represented as a Model. Irregular Troopers and REM or VH Troop Types are excluded in the ITS 17 English publication; the Spanish text omits VH.

The designated Key Ops gains [[skill:dodge|Dodge (+3)]] and [[skill:tactical-awareness|Tactical Awareness]] even if not shown on its Unit Profile. These extra Skills do not stack with existing instances. Identify the Key Ops with a Player A or B Marker.

rules.name: Threaten Key Ops
paragraphs: At the end of the game, an enemy Key Ops is Threatened when you have at least one non-Null Trooper, as a Model and not a Marker, inside that Key Ops' Zone of Control. Threatening earns 1 OP instead of (not alongside) the 2 OP for Killing the enemy Key Ops.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 85 forbids REM and VH Troop Types from Key Ops designation, but ES p. 90 names only REM. The English exclusion is retained while the bilingual difference remains unresolved.

ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 84 says Shasvastii Troopers count in Unconscious or any non-Null State. ES p. 89 instead specifies Normal or Shasvastii Embryo. Do not silently equate those state sets; the English rule is retained.

record.name: Annihilation
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Seekers Annihilation: score by enemy Army Points Killed, surviving Victory Points and the enemy Lieutenant Killed. The original English and Spanish survival bands conflict.

condition.text: Kill the enemy [[skill:lieutenant]].

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: An enemy Trooper counts as Killed after entering [[state:dead]] or if it is in a Null [[trait:state|State]] at the end of the game.
A Trooper not deployed on the table as a Model or Marker by the end of the game also counts as Killed by the adversary.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: The Retreat! rules do not apply in this scenario.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model or use the Classified Deck. The Secure HVT rule does not apply.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 81 awards 1/3/4 OP for the low/middle/high surviving Victory Point bands, while ES p. 85 prints 3/4/4 OP for those same numerical bands. The English chart is retained, not silently reconciled with the Spanish table.

ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 82 prints [[distance:8:inch]] x [[distance:32:cm]] as the 150-point Deployment Zone size; its own diagram instead depicts an [[distance:8:inch]]-deep zone spanning the [[distance:24:inch]] table width. ES p. 86 prints [[distance:20:cm]] x [[distance:60:cm]] and shows that geometry. Retain the reviewed map, not an invented mixed-unit zone.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 81 and ES p. 85 award 3 OP for 176-274 enemy Army Points Killed and 4 OP for more than 275, leaving exactly 275 without a printed award.

ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 81 and ES p. 85 print 176-274 and more than 275 surviving Victory Points for adjacent bands, leaving exactly 275 without a printed award. The language editions additionally disagree on the awarded OP as documented separately.

record.name: Cutthroat
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Cutthroat: Kill enemy Army Points and Lieutenants, Kill the enemy Key Ops and exceed their Key Ops' Trooper kills. Reinforced Tactical Link replaces Loss of Lieutenant.

objectives.name: Kill the same number of enemy Lieutenants

condition.text: Kill the same number of enemy [[skill:lieutenant|Lieutenants]] as the opponent, provided this player killed at least one enemy Lieutenant.
Kill the opposing Key Ops: the selected Trooper is Killed under the mission's Killing criteria.

Kill more enemy Troopers with your Key Ops than the opposing player kills with theirs. Credit a Key Ops when they cause a Trooper to be in a Null State at game end, or cause Wounds/STR loss during the Order in which that Trooper enters Dead State.

rules.name: Reinforced Tactical Link
paragraphs: The [[rule:loss-of-lieutenant|Loss of Lieutenant]] rule does not apply in this mission.
The identity of every Lieutenant is Open Information, including which Marker represents them while Camouflaged, Decoyed or using Holoprojector.
A Lieutenant must be placed on the game table as a Model or Marker at the beginning of Game Round 1. Hidden Deployment is not permitted for the Lieutenant.

During the Tactical Phase of their Active Turn, a player without an eligible Lieutenant because the current Lieutenant is undeployed, Isolated or in a Null State must name a replacement without spending an Order. The new Lieutenant's identity is also Open Information, and the replacement must be on the game table as a Model or Marker.

rules.name: Key Ops
paragraphs: At the end of the Deployment Phase, in Initiative order, each player designates one Key Ops from their Army List. The Trooper must be deployed on the table as a Model, not in Hidden Deployment or Marker State, and must remain a Model.
Irregular Troopers and REM or VH Troop Types cannot become Key Ops under the English ITS 17 text; the Spanish source omits the VH restriction.

The Key Ops gains [[skill:dodge|Dodge (+3)]] and [[skill:tactical-awareness|Tactical Awareness]], even if not in their Unit Profile. These do not stack with already possessed instances. Identify the Key Ops with the Player A or B Marker.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: An enemy Trooper is considered Killed when it enters Dead State or is in a Null State at the end of the game.
A Trooper not deployed on the game table as a Model or Marker by the end of the game counts as Killed by the adversary.
The Key Ops counts as Killing a target if they cause it to end in a Null State or cause a loss of Wounds/STR in the Order in which it enters Dead State.
A Trooper counts as a Killed Lieutenant if they held the Lieutenant role at any time during the game and enter Dead State or are in a Null State at the end of the game.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: The Retreat! rules do not apply in this mission.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model or use the Classified Deck. The Secure HVT rule does not apply.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 87 excludes REM and VH from Key Ops designation, while ES p. 92 excludes REM but omits VH. Retain the English exclusion and flag the disagreement.

ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 91 adds a condition requiring at least one Lieutenant Killed to the more-Lieutenants objective, which EN p. 86 does not explicitly state. Retain the English objective wording and the language difference.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 88 counts Troopers that were Lieutenants at any time as Killed Lieutenants if Dead or Null at game end; ES p. 93 omits that explicit sentence.

record.name: Superiority
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Superiority: dominate more Quadrants at each round end, Hack up to three Consoles for points, and have a Dominant Key Ops at game end.

objectives.name: Dominate more Quadrants each Game Round

condition.text: At game end, have your designated Key Ops in a non-Null State within a Zone of Operations that you Dominate.

rules.name: Quadrants (ZO)
paragraphs: At the end of each Game Round, and not before, divide the central part of the table into four Quadrants as shown on the map. Each Quadrant is a Zone of Operations (ZO).

A ZO is Dominated by the player with more Victory Points in it. Count Troopers represented by Models or Markers, including Proxies and Peripherals; exclude Troopers in a Null State and Tokens representing weapons, equipment or false Holoechoes.
A Trooper is inside a ZO only when more than half its base is inside that area.

rules.name: Shasvastii
paragraphs: For purposes of Dominating a ZO, the English edition states that Troopers with [[skill:shasvastii|Shasvastii]] count while Unconscious or in any non-Null State. The Spanish edition instead names Normal and Shasvastii-Embryo States. The source difference is noted below.

rules.name: Baggage
paragraphs: A Trooper with [[equipment:baggage|Baggage]] inside a ZO adds 20 Victory Points toward Dominating that ZO while it is not in a Null State.

rules.name: Consoles
paragraphs: Four Consoles stand in the center of the four Quadrants. Use a Console A Token or a piece of scenery of the same diameter; The ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart specifies 40 mm for Console Tokens.

rules.name: Hack Consoles

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console to declare Hack Consoles.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Hack the Console; failed attempts can be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
Either player can Hack a Console the opponent has already Hacked. Both then count it as Hacked for their own end-of-game Objective Points. Track each player's success with separate Player Tokens.

paragraphs: Hack Consoles is an Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console may make a Normal WIP Roll to Hack it; failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.

The opposing player may Hack a previously Hacked Console. Both players then count the Console as Hacked for their end-of-game Objective Points; use different Player Tokens to track each player's success.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved to Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: When a Specialist Troop fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, its next consecutive Order with the same Skill and target gains +3 to the WIP Roll. The third and subsequent consecutive Orders gain +3 and +1SD; these MODs stack with other applicable Scenario Skill MODs.
This sequence resets after success, using a different Skill or target, or spending an Order on another Trooper. Only one sequence per Trooper and per Scenario-labelled Skill may apply at once.

rules.name: HVT and Classified Deck not used
paragraphs: Players do not deploy an HVT Model, Secure HVT does not apply, and the Classified Deck is not used in this mission.

rules.name: Key Ops
paragraphs: At the end of Deployment, in Initiative order, each player designates a Key Ops from their Army List, deployed and remaining on the table as a Model, not a Marker or in Hidden Deployment.
Irregular Troopers and REM or VH Troop Types cannot be designated in the English ITS 17 source. The Spanish version excludes Irregular and REM but does not mention VH.
The Key Ops gains [[skill:dodge|Dodge (+3)]] and [[skill:tactical-awareness|Tactical Awareness]]; extra instances do not stack. Identify the Key Ops with a Player A or B Marker.

rules.name: Dominant Key Ops
paragraphs: A player has a Dominant Key Ops at the end of the game when that Key Ops is in any non-Null State within a Zone of Operations Dominated by that player.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 90 counts Shasvastii Troopers in Unconscious or any non-Null State, whereas ES p. 95 names Normal or Shasvastii Embryo. The English wording is retained; do not silently equate the state sets.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 92 excludes Irregular, REM and VH Troopers as Key Ops; ES p. 97 omits VH. Preserve the English exclusion and record the bilingual gap.

record.name: Provisioning
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Provisioning: extract four Supply Boxes from three Tech-Coffins, secure player-placed Safe Areas, and score end-game Control with one Classified Objective.

condition.text: Score 1 Objective Point for each Supply Box Controlled at game end, to a maximum of four. Boxes carried by eligible non-Null Models and Boxes Controlled in a Safe Area count according to this mission's Control rules.

objectives.name: Compare Supply Boxes in Safe Areas

condition.text: Control more Supply Boxes in your own Safe Area than the opponent Controls in theirs at game end.
Control the same number of Supply Boxes in each player's own Safe Area at game end, provided at least one Supply Box is Controlled in a Safe Area.
At game end, the opponent Controls no Supply Boxes in their own Safe Area. This objective does not require you to Control a Box in yours.
Complete your one Classified Objective for 1 Objective Point.

rules.name: Deployment and Tech-Coffins
paragraphs: Both sides deploy in opposite corner quarter-circle Deployment Zones shown on the three game-size maps. A Trooper may not deploy in Silhouette contact with a Tech-Coffin.

Three Tech-Coffins lie along the central diagonal, one at the table center and two [[distance:8:inch]] / [[distance:12:inch]] / [[distance:16:inch]] from it in 150 / 200–250 / 300–400-point games. Each outer Tech-Coffin contains one Supply Box and the central one contains two. Use a Tech-Coffin Marker or a scenery piece of equal diameter; the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart specifies a 40 mm Tech-Coffin Token.

rules.name: Extract Supply Boxes (Short Skill)

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in contact with a Tech-Coffin.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Extract one Supply Box. On success place a Supply Box Token beside the Trooper. Failed attempts can be retried with another Short Skill.
The central Tech-Coffin contains two Supply Boxes; each outer Tech-Coffin contains one.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 EN p. 74 requires base contact with a Tech-Coffin, while ES p. 71 requires Silhouette contact. The historical requirement preserves this unresolved language distinction.
Both ITS 17 editions require marking a Tech-Coffin with a Player A/B Token once all its Supply Boxes are extracted; neither directs removal of the emptied Tech-Coffin Token.

paragraphs: A Specialist Troop in contact with a Tech-Coffin can make a Normal WIP Roll to Extract a Supply Box, placing a Supply Box Token beside the Trooper on success. A failed Roll can be retried with another Short Skill.

Once all Supply Boxes have been Extracted from a Tech-Coffin, place a Player A or B Token beside it to mark the extraction. Unlike ITS 18 English, the ITS 17 mission does not direct removal of the emptied Tech-Coffin Token.

rules.name: Pick Up Supply Boxes (Short Skill)
paragraphs: A Trooper in Silhouette contact with an uncarried Supply Box, or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying it, may pick it up without a Roll outside the stricter Safe Area case. The usual Supply Box carrying rules apply.

If the Supply Box is in the enemy's Safe Area, only a Specialist Troop may pick it up, requiring a Normal WIP-3 Roll. Both ITS 17 editions specifically name the opposing player's Safe Area; do not apply the broader ITS 18 English 'any Safe Area' wording.

rules.name: Common Supply Box Rules
paragraphs: Each Model can carry a maximum of one Supply Box, or two with Baggage. Only Models, not Markers, carry Boxes. Keep each carried Supply Box Token in Silhouette contact with its carrier.
If a carrier enters or is in a Null State, it drops its Box slightly out of Silhouette contact. Supply Box Tokens do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Control Supply Boxes
paragraphs: A Supply Box is Controlled at game end if carried by your Model (not a Marker) that is neither in a Null State nor in Silhouette contact with an enemy Model. Boxes deposited in your Safe Area are considered Controlled unless successfully picked up by an enemy Specialist.

Score one point per Controlled Supply Box, compare the counts in each player's own Safe Area for the 3-point greater-than or 1-point nonzero-tie award, and gain another 2 points if the opponent Controls no Boxes in their own Safe Area.

rules.name: Player-Placed Safe Areas
paragraphs: Before Deployment each player places one Circular Template ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter) on a surface at least the size of that Template, wholly outside all Deployment Zones and not overlapping the other Safe Area. The player who kept Deployment places first.

These are player-placed Circular Templates, not fixed map objects. A Trooper can deposit a Supply Box in their Safe Area with a Short Skill and no Roll, placing the Box completely inside the Safe Area. Both ITS 17 languages require the Box to be wholly inside.
Only Specialist Troops may recover a Supply Box from the enemy's Safe Area using Pick Up Supply Boxes and a WIP-3 Roll.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] qualify as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers may not use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: Operational Learning
paragraphs: A Specialist Troop that fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill gains +3 WIP on the next consecutive Order attempting the same Skill against the same target; from the third consecutive Order onward it gains +3 WIP and +1 Success Die. Other applicable Scenario Skill MODs still apply.

Success, a different Skill or target, a break in consecutive Orders, or spending an Order on a different Trooper resets the sequence. Only one sequence per Trooper and Scenario Skill is active at a time.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 74 requires base contact to Extract from a Tech-Coffin; ES p. 71 says Silhouette contact. The terms are not assumed equivalent in the historical record.

record.name: Area of Interest
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Area of Interest: Dominate player-placed Areas and the Special Area, Activate the central Antenna each round, and choose between a Classified Objective and INTELCOM.

condition.text: At the end of the game, score 1 Objective Point for each of the three player-placed Areas of Interest you Dominate, up to 3 Objective Points. The Special Area also counts as one of these three Areas.
At the end of each Game Round, score 1 Objective Point if you Dominate the player-designated Special Area of Interest, up to 3 Objective Points across three Game Rounds.
At the end of each Game Round, score 1 Objective Point if the center Communication Antenna is Activated for you, up to 3 Objective Points across three Game Rounds.
Complete your one Classified Objective for 1 Objective Point if you chose to use the selected card as a Classified Objective rather than as an INTELCOM Card.

rules.name: Deployment and Initial Placement
paragraphs: Both sides deploy in opposite corner quarter-circle Deployment Zones sized for the game. No Trooper may deploy inside an Area of Interest or in Silhouette contact with the central Communication Antenna.

Three Areas of Interest are positioned by players before Deployment, not fixed on the published map. Their Circular Templates must be on suitable surfaces, wholly outside Deployment Zones, and must not overlap.

rules.name: Communication Antenna
paragraphs: One Communication Antenna stands at the table center, represented by a Transmission Antenna Token (TRANS. ANTENNA) or scenery of matching diameter. ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 specifies a 40 mm Transmission Antenna Token and 25 mm Player A/B Tokens. Player A/B Tokens can mark its current Activation.
The Antenna may be Activated repeatedly by either player; activating it for your player replaces the opponent's activation.

rules.name: Activate Communication Antenna (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Communication Antenna may declare this Skill.
effects: Normally Activation requires no Roll. If an enemy Hacker is in any Area of Interest, one eligible enemy Hacker may oppose it with an ARO, resulting in a Face to Face WIP Roll.
A failed attempt may be repeated with another Short Skill.
At the end of the Game Round, the player with the current Activation earns 1 Objective Point.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 EN p. 78 says one enemy Hacker within an Area of Interest can oppose with an ARO; ES p. 82 requires selecting one Hacker. The mandatory/optional distinction is unresolved.
ITS 17 ES p. 82 calls the Antenna Connected on initial activation but Activated when describing later changes of control; the EN edition consistently calls it Activated.

paragraphs: Only Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with the Communication Antenna may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Normally Activation requires no Roll.

An enemy Hacker within an Area of Interest can oppose an Activation with an ARO, making a Face to Face WIP Roll. ITS 17 Spanish requires choosing a Hacker for this ARO; English uses optional wording. A failed attempt can be repeated.
At the end of each Game Round the player whose Activation is current earns 1 Objective Point.

rules.name: Player-Placed Areas of Interest
paragraphs: There are three Circular Template Areas of Interest ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter each; Zones of Operations); one is the Special Area of Interest. They are not pre-positioned map elements.

Before Deployment and in Initiative order, the first-turn player places one ordinary Area and the Special Area, designating the Special Area at placement. The second-turn player places the remaining ordinary Area.
Each Area must fit on a surface at least as large as its Circular Template, completely outside every Deployment Zone, without overlapping any other Area of Interest.

rules.name: Dominate Zones of Operations
paragraphs: A player Dominates an Area of Interest when they have more Victory Points from eligible Troops inside that Area than their opponent. More than half of a Trooper's base must lie within the Area.

Eligible Troops include Models, Markers representing Troopers, Proxies, and Peripherals. Troops in Null States, fake Holoechoes, weapons or equipment Tokens, and Tokens not representing Troops do not count.

ITS 17 English counts Troopers with [[skill:shasvastii|Shasvastii]] while Unconscious or in any non-Null State; Spanish names Normal or Unconscious. This bilingual state-set distinction is unresolved. Non-Null Troopers with [[equipment:baggage|Baggage]] add 20 Victory Points for Domination.
At game end, earn 1 Objective Point per Area Dominated, maximum 3; each Game Round, Dominate the Special Area for another 1 Objective Point.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and Troops with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors, and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform Specialist-only tasks.

rules.name: INTELCOM Card (Support and Control)
paragraphs: Before the game and after choosing the first Classified Objective, each player decides whether the selected card is their Classified Objective or an INTELCOM Card. Both players roll a die; the higher roller announces that choice first. The card's contents remain Private Information.

At game-end scoring, in Initiative order, a player using INTELCOM in Support and Control Mode may add that card's numeric value to their Victory Points in one chosen Area of Interest, provided they have at least one non-Null Trooper inside that Area.

INTELCOM adds Victory Points in the chosen Area of Interest rather than awarding Objective Points directly. ITS 17 EN p. 80 places this at the end of the last Game Round, whereas ES pp. 83–84 explicitly name the third Game Round; Retreat! may end the game earlier.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, this mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 77 explicitly marks Area of Interest suitable for Reinforcements (YES), but ES p. 80 explicitly states NO. Do not select one language as an unqualified season-wide permission.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 78 permits one enemy Hacker inside an Area of Interest to declare an ARO; ES p. 82 requires choosing one enemy Hacker for the ARO.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 79 counts Shasvastii Troopers Unconscious or in any non-Null State; ES p. 83 specifies Normal or Unconscious. The state sets must not be silently equated.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 80 allows INTELCOM at the end of the last Game Round; ES pp. 83–84 name the end of the third Game Round even though Retreat! can end the mission earlier.
ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 82 says the Antenna is Conectada on a successful activation but Activada when describing control changes. EN p. 78 uses Activated.

record.name: Last Launch
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Last Launch: download and transfer IDs, extract identified Troopers from the Launching Tower, and score extracted points, Specialists, Tower Domination and three Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, your total Extracted Army Points exceeds the opponent's total. Extracted Baggage Troops add 20 points to their contributing total.
At game end, your number of Extracted Specialist Troops exceeds the opponent's.
At game end, the number of the opponent's Specialist Troops you have Killed exceeds the number of your Specialist Troops Killed by the opponent.
At game end, both players have Killed the same number of opposing Specialist Troops. This 1-point tie award is an alternative to the 2-point greater-than award.
At game end, Dominate the central Launching Tower Zone of Operations by having more eligible Victory Points inside than the opponent.
Complete each of your three Classified Objectives for 1 Objective Point each, up to 3.

rules.name: Deployment and Launching Tower
paragraphs: Both sides deploy in opposite edge Deployment Zones of game-size-specific depth, and no Trooper can deploy inside the centrally located Launching Tower.

The Launching Tower is a [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]] Zone of Operations at the table center. Its walls count as infinitely high and completely block Line of Fire. Four Wide Gates are centered in its four walls and start open; the published diagram is schematic and does not specify their opening width.

ITS 17 EN p. 65 specifies an [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]] Launching Tower; ES p. 77 says [[distance:20:cm]] × [[distance:20:cm]]. This small unit difference is preserved as a bilingual source issue.

rules.name: ID Scanners
paragraphs: Two ID Scanners stand along the table centerline, each [[distance:4:inch]] from the table edge at 150 points and [[distance:8:inch]] otherwise (ES: [[distance:10:cm]] / [[distance:20:cm]]). Represent each with a Tech-Coffin Token or scenery of matching diameter. The ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart specifies a 40 mm Tech-Coffin Token.

rules.name: Download ID (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an ID Scanner may declare this Skill.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll. On success place an ID Token beside the Trooper. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.

paragraphs: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with an ID Scanner may use this Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Normal WIP Roll downloads an ID on success; place one ID Token beside the Trooper.
Each failed attempt can be retried by spending another Short Skill and rolling again.

rules.name: Swap ID (Short Skill)

requirements: A Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with an allied Trooper carrying an ID Token.
effects: Spend an Attack, Scenario Short Skill to transfer the ID without a Roll. Place the ID Token beside the recipient.
restrictions: An ID carrier may not enter or remain in a Marker State. Each Trooper may carry at most one ID Token. Remove the Token if its carrier enters Dead State.

paragraphs: A Trooper in Silhouette contact with an allied Trooper carrying an ID Token may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill to transfer the ID without a Roll. Place the Token beside the recipient.
An ID carrier may not enter or be in a Marker State. Each Trooper may have at most one ID Token. Remove the Token if its carrier enters Dead State.

rules.name: Wide Gates
paragraphs: The Launching Tower has four Wide Gates centered on its walls, open at the start. ITS 17 ES p. 77 also explicitly requires Wide Gate Tokens or equivalent scenery and allows access regardless of Silhouette; EN p. 65 does not state that extra clause.
The map shows the Tower's exterior square and the central ID Checker. Gate locations are described here because the source does not provide a numerical gate width for geometric placement.

rules.name: Dominate the Launching Tower ZO
paragraphs: Dominate the Zone of Operations by having more Victory Points from eligible Troops inside the Tower than the opponent. Models, Markers representing Troops, Proxies and Peripherals count; non-Troop Tokens, fake Holoechoes and Troops in Null States do not.

A Trooper is inside the Tower if more than half its base lies inside. ITS 17 EN p. 65 counts Shasvastii Troopers in Unconscious or any non-Null State; ES p. 78 names Normal or Unconscious. The difference is unresolved.
Each non-Null Baggage Trooper inside the Tower provides an extra 20 Victory Points for this Domination comparison.

rules.name: ID Checker
paragraphs: One ID Checker stands at the center of the Launching Tower. Represent it with a Console A Token or a piece of matching-diameter scenery; The ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart specifies a 40 mm Console Token.

rules.name: Extract Identified Trooper (Short Skill)

requirements: A Trooper carrying an ID Token must be in Silhouette contact with the central ID Checker.
effects: Extraction succeeds without a Roll. Remove the Trooper and any of its Peripherals inside the Launching Tower from the table.
Add the removed Troopers' points to the player's Extracted Army Points. Extracted Troopers continue contributing Victory Points even if they enter Null or Dead State during that extraction Order.
A previously Extracted Lieutenant triggers Loss of Lieutenant during its player's Tactical Phase.
restrictions: A Trooper participating in a Coordinated Order cannot declare this Skill.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 EN p. 66 refers to adding the removed Troopers' points (plural, including Peripherals removed inside the Tower), while ES p. 79 says the removed Trooper's cost (singular). Whether Peripheral costs contribute is not explicitly equivalent.

paragraphs: A Trooper carrying an ID Token and in Silhouette contact with the central ID Checker may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill, unless participating in a Coordinated Order. Extraction succeeds without a Roll.

Remove the extracting Trooper and any of its Peripherals inside the Launching Tower. Extracted Army Points are Open Information; ITS 17 EN p. 66 refers to the removed Troopers' points, while ES p. 79 refers to the extracting Trooper's points alone. The Peripheral-cost interpretation remains unresolved.

Extracted Troops continue contributing to their owner's Victory Points, even if they entered a Null or Dead State during the Order they were Extracted. A previously Extracted Lieutenant triggers the normal Loss of Lieutenant rule during the player's Tactical Phase.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: An opposing Trooper is considered Killed if it enters Dead State, remains in a Null State at game end, or has not been deployed as a Model or Marker by game end.
Extracted Troops are never considered Killed by the adversary, even if removed from the table.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models to perform Specialist-only tasks.

rules.name: Baggage and Extracted Points
paragraphs: Every Extracted Baggage Trooper adds 20 extra points to the total Extracted Army Points, in addition to its own points cost. Non-Null Baggage Troops inside the Tower also add 20 Victory Points for Domination.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: Retreat! rules do not apply in this mission. The game ends after the third Game Round, without the usual Retreat! early-ending condition.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 65 specifies an [[distance:8:inch]] × [[distance:8:inch]] Launching Tower; ES p. 77 gives [[distance:20:cm]] × [[distance:20:cm]]. Geometry uses the English dimensions without declaring these exact equivalents.
ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 77 requires Wide Gate Tokens or similar scenery and explicitly allows any Silhouette to pass. EN p. 65 only states that four Wide Gates start open.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 65 counts Shasvastii Troopers while Unconscious or in any non-Null State; ES p. 78 specifically names Normal or Unconscious.

ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 66 adds the removed Troopers' points after extracting a Trooper and its Peripherals inside the Tower; ES p. 79 refers to the removed Trooper's points in the singular. Whether Peripheral points count is not explicitly identical.

record.name: B-Pong
record.summary: ITS Season 17 B-Pong: reposition the central Tracking Beacon toward the enemy half, Control it and a Console each round, and complete two Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, the entire Tracking Beacon is inside the opponent's half of the table. The initial center position does not qualify.
For each of your two completed Classified Objectives, score 1 Objective Point (up to 2).

rules.name: Forces, Deployment, and Exclusion Zone
paragraphs: Both players deploy in opposing table-edge Deployment Zones: [[distance:12:inch]] deep in 150-point games and [[distance:16:inch]] deep in 200–400-point games. Table dimensions for each game size are shown on the map.

The Exclusion Zone extends [[distance:2:inch]] either side of the centerline at 150 points, and [[distance:4:inch]] either side at 200–400 points. Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy within it.

The Beacon starts at the table center and can subsequently be moved by scenario actions. Two Consoles stand on the centerline at [[distance:6:inch]] / [[distance:8:inch]] / [[distance:12:inch]] from each table edge in 150 / 200–250 / 300–400-point games respectively.

rules.name: Tracking Beacon
paragraphs: One Tracking Beacon begins at the table center and is represented by a Beacon Token or equivalent scenery of matching diameter. ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 lists the Beacon Token at 25 mm, not 40 mm.

At the end of each Game Round, a player Controls the Beacon only if they alone have a non-Null Trooper Model, not a Marker, in Silhouette contact and no enemy Trooper is in contact. Both ITS 17 language editions use end-of-round timing.

rules.name: Relocate the Tracking Beacon

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Tracking Beacon may declare this Skill.
effects: Spend one Short Skill without a Roll to place the Tracking Beacon anywhere within [[distance:4:inch]] of its previous position (ES [[distance:10:cm]]).
restrictions: A Specialist Troop may declare this Skill only once per Game Round.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Tracking Beacon may declare this Skill, once per Game Round.

Without a Roll, place the Beacon anywhere within [[distance:4:inch]] of its previous position (ES [[distance:10:cm]]). Both ITS 17 originals measure from the Beacon's old position, not from the declaring Trooper.

rules.name: Tracking Beacon Movement
paragraphs: The Beacon's destination must be fully supported by a nonvertical surface. An unobstructed traversable path must connect its starting and ending positions; impassable walls, sealed rooms and gaps too small for its diameter prevent relocation.
Place the Tracking Beacon in its new position at the Conclusion of the Order. Its movement is not restricted to the initial map center.

rules.name: Activate Console

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in contact with a Console.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate the Console; failed attempts can be repeated by spending another Short Skill.

On success choose to Nudge the Tracking Beacon within [[distance:2:inch]] of its position, or Magnetize it up to [[distance:6:inch]] directly toward the table center, without crossing the center, per ITS 17 English.
restrictions: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console may declare this Skill. The Beacon cannot be in Silhouette contact with a Trooper. Each Specialist Troop may successfully Activate a Console only once per Game Round. Both ITS 17 English and Spanish impose these requirements.
clarifications: ITS 17 ES p. 41 describes moving the Beacon [[distance:15:cm]] toward the center, rather than up to that distance in the English version.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 ES p. 41 calls a successfully Activated Console 'Conectada' (Connected) despite titling the Skill 'Activar Consola'; EN p. 39 uses Activated.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with a Console may make a Normal WIP Roll to Activate it; failed attempts can be retried with another Short Skill.
The Beacon cannot be in Silhouette contact with any Trooper. Each Specialist Troop may successfully Activate a Console only once per Game Round. Both ITS 17 editions state these limits.

On success choose to Nudge the Beacon within [[distance:2:inch]] (ES [[distance:5:cm]]) of its position, or Magnetize it up to [[distance:6:inch]] toward the center, without passing it. Spanish uses [[distance:15:cm]] toward the center without explicitly saying 'up to', and calls successful Activation 'Connected'; these wording distinctions remain unresolved.

rules.name: Control a Console
paragraphs: At the end of each Game Round, a Console is Controlled when a player is the only player with at least one non-Null Trooper as a Model (not a Marker) in Silhouette contact with it. Any opposing Troopers in contact prevent Control.
Controlling either or both Consoles scores just 1 Objective Point per Game Round. Activation itself does not count as Control.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, or Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

rules.name: No Quarter
paragraphs: Retreat! rules do not apply in B-Pong. The mission lasts all three Game Rounds.

rules.name: Classified Objectives
paragraphs: Each player has two Classified Objectives, each worth 1 Objective Point when completed.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 39 permits placing the Beacon within [[distance:6:inch]] of its previous position toward the center; ES p. 41 specifies [[distance:15:cm]] toward the center without explicitly treating it as a maximum.
ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 41 describes successful Console activation as 'Conectada' while the action is 'Activar Consola'. EN p. 39 consistently says Activated.

record.name: Crossing Lines
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Crossing Lines: Dominate both Dead Zones across a split deployment, Activate the two Antennas, and score without Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At the end of the game, Dominate both Dead Zones.

rules.name: Deployment and Exclusion Zones
paragraphs: Each player has a rear Deployment Zone and a second Deployment Zone in the opposing half of the table, inside the central strip. Up to 75 Army Points of Troops can deploy in the central strip. Both forward Zones are [[distance:4:inch]] deep (ES [[distance:10:cm]]).
Two Dead Zones between the Deployment Zones are Exclusion Zones. Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy inside them.
No Trooper may deploy in Silhouette contact with an Antenna. Superior Deployment Skills are prohibited except Impersonation.

rules.name: Dominate a Zone of Operations
paragraphs: A player Dominates a Zone of Operations if they have more Victory Points of eligible Troopers inside than their opponent.
Count Models, Trooper Markers, Proxies and Peripheral Troops in non-Null States. Equipment Tokens and fake Holoechoes do not count; more than half of a Trooper's base must lie within the Zone.

ITS 17 EN p. 53 says Shasvastii Troops inside the ZO count while in Shasvastii-Embryo or any non-Null State; ES p. 44 specifies Normal or Unconscious instead. Baggage Troops in non-Null States add 20 Victory Points to Domination.

rules.name: Activate Antenna

requirements: Only Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with an Antenna may declare Activate Antenna.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to activate the Antenna for that player. Failed attempts can be retried.
The opponent can activate an Antenna again, replacing the previous player's ownership Token.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 53 represents Antennas with Transmission Antenna Tokens; ES p. 44 says Console A Tokens. Both say matching-diameter scenery; both types are 40 mm under the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart; the naming conflict remains.

paragraphs: Two Antennas are positioned on the centerline, [[distance:6:inch]] / [[distance:8:inch]] / [[distance:12:inch]] from the table edges at 150 / 200–250 / 300–400 points respectively. ITS 17 EN p. 53 requires a Transmission Antenna Token or matching-diameter scenery; ES p. 44 instead specifies a Console A Token or equivalent same-diameter scenery. Both Token types are 40 mm under the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart.
Only Specialist Troops in Silhouette contact with an Antenna may use the Activate Antenna Short Skill: a successful Normal WIP Roll activates it for that player; failed attempts may be retried.
An Antenna can be activated by the opponent, replacing the previous player's ownership Token.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Troopers with Chain of Command, and Specialist Operatives qualify as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist tasks.

rules.name: Secure HVT and Secure Treasure not used
paragraphs: There are no Classified Objectives in ITS 17 Crossing Lines. The mission explicitly does not apply Secure HVT or Secure Treasure (EN p. 54 / ES p. 45).

Unlike ITS 18, ITS 17 does not explicitly say that the HVT Model must not be deployed or that the Classified Deck is not used. The zero-HVT play-context projection is retained provisionally and this source gap is recorded for verification.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 EN pp. 51-52 describe central strips of [[distance:4:inch]] × [[distance:32:inch]] at 150 points and [[distance:4:inch]] × [[distance:48:inch]] at 200/250 points, whereas ES p. 42 describes [[distance:10:cm]] × [[distance:60:cm]] and [[distance:10:cm]] × [[distance:80:cm]] respectively. The English strip length conflicts with table width. Geometry follows the Spanish widths and published layout.
ITS 17 EN p. 53 counts Shasvastii Troops in Shasvastii-Embryo or any non-Null State; ES p. 44 says Normal or Unconscious. The formulations differ.

ITS 17 EN p. 53 represents an Antenna with a Transmission Antenna Token; ES p. 44 instead says Console A Token. Both allow scenery matching that Token's diameter both Token types are 40 mm under the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart, despite the naming conflict.

ITS 17 EN p. 54 / ES p. 45 disable Secure HVT and Secure Treasure but do not explicitly prohibit HVT Model deployment. The no-HVT play-context count follows the existing edition's schema and needs source verification; ITS 18's explicit no-HVT/no-Classified-Deck clause cannot be attributed to ITS 17.

record.name: Corporate Appropriation
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Corporate Appropriation: Capture or Destroy Prototypes, collect Panoply equipment and complete three Classified Objectives.

condition.text: At game end, a non-Null Model (not Marker) carries the enemy Prototype without disqualifying enemy Silhouette contact. EN p. 43 says any enemy Model; ES p. 35 disregards Null-state Models. Preserve the bilingual source issue.
In addition to the 2-point Capture objective, at game end have the enemy Prototype Captured by a qualifying Model inside your own Deployment Zone.
At game end your own Prototype is Destroyed. This is the alternative 3-point outcome for your own Prototype, rather than the 1-point non-captured and non-destroyed award.
At game end, your own Prototype has neither been Destroyed nor Captured by the enemy. This 1-point award is exclusive of the 3-point Destroyed outcome.
At game end, your Troops have obtained more weapons or pieces of equipment from the two Panoplies than the opponent.
Each completed Classified Objective is worth one point; three Classified Objectives per player, up to 3 points.

rules.name: Forces, Deployment and Exclusion
paragraphs: Players deploy along opposite table edges within the source's game-size-specific Deployment Zones. A central Exclusion Zone spans [[distance:4:inch]] on either side of the table's central horizontal line; Airborne Deployment (AD) and Superior Deployment cannot be used to deploy inside it.
The two Prototypes are fixed on the centerline at quarter-width points; the two Panoplies lie on the inner edges of Deployment Zones at table mid-width.

rules.name: Prototype Profile
paragraphs: Two Prototypes stand on the centerline at [[distance:6:inch]] / [[distance:8:inch]] / [[distance:12:inch]] from the table edges at 150 / 200–250 / 300–400 points. Before deployment, the second-turn player assigns which belongs to each side. Represent them with Objective Tokens or scenery of matching diameter; ITS 17 does not specify a 40 mm footprint.

Each Prototype has ARM 6, BTS 6, STR 3 and S 3, with Fixed CC Roll 8 and GizmoKit (PH 9). Both ITS 17 EN p. 41 and ES p. 33 allow targeting a Prototype only if no allied or enemy Trooper would also be affected by the Attack.

rules.name: Automated Defense System (ADS)
paragraphs: Each CC Attack against a Prototype triggers a Face to Face ADS CC Attack with a fixed Roll of 8. ITS 17 EN p. 42 and ES p. 34 both prohibit applying any MODs to the attacker's CC Attribute.
A successful ADS Roll imposes a Stun Ammunition hit, PS 5, requiring one BTS Saving Roll. Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not protect against this hit.

rules.name: Destroy Prototypes
paragraphs: Prototypes can be damaged only by CC Attacks with the Anti-materiel Trait or by D-Charges. A Prototype is Destroyed and removed once Wounds taken reach its STR 3. The Engineer Special Skill or GizmoKit may be used on Prototypes.
No Attacks against Prototypes can be declared during the first Game Round, except Pick Up Prototype.

rules.name: Pick Up Prototype

requirements: A Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with an unattended enemy Prototype Token or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying the enemy Prototype.
effects: Spend one Attack, Scenario Short Skill to pick up the enemy Prototype without a Roll.
restrictions: Troopers may pick up only the enemy Prototype; follow the Common Rules of Prototypes.

paragraphs: Any Trooper in Silhouette contact with an unattended enemy Prototype Token, or an allied Trooper in Normal State carrying that enemy Prototype, can pick it up with one Attack, Scenario Short Skill without a Roll.
A Trooper may only pick up the enemy Prototype and must obey the Common Rules of Prototypes.

rules.name: Common Rules of Prototypes
paragraphs: Carriers cannot declare Move as the second Basic Short Skill of an Order except with Baggage. ITS 17 EN p. 43 calls Baggage a Special Skill; ES p. 35 calls it Equipment. Only Models, not Markers, can carry Prototypes.

A carried Prototype Token always remains on the table and in Silhouette contact with its carrier. A carrier entering or in a Null State drops the Prototype just outside contact. Prototype Tokens do not block movement or Line of Fire.

rules.name: Capturing Enemy Prototype
paragraphs: A player Captures the enemy Prototype at game end when a non-Null Model, not a Marker, carries it. ITS 17 EN p. 43 disallows contact with any enemy Model; ES p. 35 says enemy Trooper contact and explicitly disregards Null-state Models. The exact enemy-contact scope remains a source issue.

rules.name: Panoplies
paragraphs: Two Panoplies, one in each table half, are at the midpoint of the forward boundary of each Deployment Zone. Use an Objective Token or matching-diameter scenery; The ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart gives the Objective Token a 40 mm diameter.
A Trooper in Silhouette contact with a Panoply can spend one Short Skill to cancel Unloaded State. The separate Use Panoply Short Skill governs acquiring D-Charges or other equipment.

rules.name: Use Panoply

requirements: The Trooper must be in Silhouette contact with a Panoply.
effects: With a successful Normal WIP Roll, acquire D-Charges or roll on the Panoply Chart for a weapon or item.
Troopers with Booty or another applicable Special Skill do not need to perform the WIP Roll.
If the chart yields an already-owned weapon or item, repeat that chart Roll.
restrictions: After a success, the same Trooper cannot use that Panoply again.
clarifications: An in-contact Trooper may spend one Short Skill to cancel Unloaded State; this is also described under the Panoplies rule.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 EN pp. 43–44 / ES p. 36 call this an Attack, Scenario Short Skill.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Trooper in Silhouette contact with a Panoply rolls Normal WIP to obtain D-Charges or a Panoply Chart result. A Trooper with Booty or another applicable Skill needs no WIP Roll.
A successful user cannot use that same Panoply again; duplicates from the chart may be rerolled.

rules.name: Panoply Chart (D20)
paragraphs: 1–2: +1 ARM. 3–4: Light Flamethrower. 5–6: Grenades. 7–8: DA CC Weapon. 9: Multispectral Visor L1. 10: EXP CC Weapon.
11: Adhesive Launcher Rifle. 12: TAG—Immunity (AP); other Troop Types—+2 ARM. 13: Panzerfaust. 14: Monofilament CC Weapon. 15: MOV 8-4.
16: TAG—BS Attack (Shock); other Troop Types—MULTI Rifle. 17: MULTI Sniper Rifle. 18: TAG—Immunity (ARM); other Troop Types—+4 ARM. 19: Mimetism (-6). 20: TAG—BS Attack (+1B); other Troop Types—HMG.
The English and Spanish chart results are equivalent in concept, subject to the sources' normal unit conventions.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troops with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] are Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist-only tasks.

condition.text: If a player begins an Active Turn in Retreat!, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 40 says Suitable for Reinforcements YES, while ES p. 32 says NO. This source-level conflict does not alter the independently reviewed objective facts.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 43 prohibits contact with any enemy Model for Capture; ES p. 35 says enemy Troopers and explicitly excludes Null-state Models from consideration.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 43 calls Baggage a Special Skill for the carrier's Move exception, while ES p. 35 calls Baggage a piece of Equipment. The exception itself matches.

record.name: Critical Intervention
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Critical Intervention: asymmetrical Attacker/Defender objectives for extracting a Data Pack, holding the Server Room, and commanding or bypassing its defensive turret system.

condition.text: The Attacker has Unlocked the Data Console using the Inhibitor Antenna.
The Attacker successfully Extracted the Data Pack from the central Data Console.
At game end, the Trooper that Extracted the Data Pack is not considered Killed.
At game end, the Trooper that Extracted the Data Pack is in the Attacker's own Deployment Zone and is in a non-Null State.
At game end, the Attacker Dominates the Server Room Zone of Operations.
Kill at least 40 enemy Army Points in a 150-point game.
Kill at least 50 enemy Army Points in a 200-point game.
Kill at least 65 enemy Army Points in a 250-point game.
Kill at least 75 enemy Army Points in a 300-point game.
Kill at least 85 enemy Army Points in a 350-point game.
Kill at least 100 enemy Army Points in a 400-point game.
Prevent the Attacker from Unlocking the Data Console.
Prevent the Attacker from Extracting the Data Pack.
Kill the Trooper that Extracted the Data Pack. This award applies only if the Attacker Extracted the Pack.
At game end, the Defender Dominates the Server Room Zone of Operations.
Kill at least 75 enemy Army Points in a 150-point game.
Kill at least 100 enemy Army Points in a 200-point game.
Kill at least 125 enemy Army Points in a 250-point game.
Kill at least 150 enemy Army Points in a 300-point game.
Kill at least 175 enemy Army Points in a 350-point game.
Kill at least 200 enemy Army Points in a 400-point game.
Each player may complete one Classified Objective worth 1 Objective Point; instead they may select that card for INTELCOM Support and Control.

rules.name: Attacker and Defender Roles
paragraphs: Two fixed roles apply, not a mutually chosen Main Objective set: the player taking the first Player Turn is the Attacker, and the player taking the second Player Turn is the Defender. Each has distinct Main Objectives; the Classified Objective is common.

Before Deployment, the Defender may spend one Command Token either to activate the Server Room Defense System, or instead to ignore the Server Room deployment restriction and deploy up to 65 Army Points of Troops from their Army List anywhere within the Server Room. Superior Deployment Skills are not required for that exception.
This optional Command Token spending is additional to the Strategic Use of Command Tokens. The Defender may select only one of these options with the single Token.

rules.name: Deployment and Attacker Exclusion Zone
paragraphs: Both players deploy on opposite edges within the game-size-specific Deployment Zones. The Server Room is a No Deployment area unless the Defender spends the special Command Token on the room-deployment exception.

A central Exclusion Zone extends [[distance:4:inch]] on either side of the table's central line. Airborne Deployment (AD) or Superior Deployment Skills cannot be used to deploy inside that Zone; the source labels this as the Attacker's Exclusion Zone.

rules.name: Server Room and Gates
paragraphs: The central Server Room is a Zone of Operations measuring [[distance:8:inch]] square in ITS 17 EN p. 47, or [[distance:20:cm]] square in ES p. 65. Its infinitely high walls block Line of Fire; four Wide Gates centered on the walls are open at the start of the game.

Use Wide Gate Tokens or equal-size scenery (EN p. 47, ES p. 66). ITS 17 ES p. 66 additionally states that any Silhouette may access the room through these Gates. A numerical Gate width is not specified; the source map only places the openings.

rules.name: Dominate the Server Room ZO
paragraphs: To Dominate the Server Room ZO, a player must have more Victory Points of eligible Troopers inside than the opponent. Models, Trooper Markers, Proxies and Peripheral Troops count; Null-state Troops, non-Trooper equipment Tokens and fake Holoechoes do not.
A Trooper is inside when more than half their base is inside. ITS 17 EN p. 47 includes Shasvastii-Embryo or any non-Null State; ES p. 66 specifically names Normal or Unconscious.
A non-Null Baggage Trooper inside the Server Room adds 20 Victory Points for the Domination comparison.

rules.name: Server Room Defense System
paragraphs: Two Armed Turrets in different Server Room corners are represented by Defensive Turret A/B Tokens or Models/scenery of matching Silhouette (ITS 17 EN p. 48 / ES pp. 66–67). Turret positions are schematic; no footprint or corner clearance is specified.

When active, the Server Room Defense System reacts with BS or CC Attacks to Orders declared by active enemy Models (not Markers) in Line of Fire or Silhouette contact. Both ITS 17 languages say 'enemy Models', not specifically Attacker Models.
Both originals print CC 5, BS 10, WIP 11, ARM 2, BTS 3, STR 1, S 2, 360° Visor, Total Reaction, Combi Rifle, and PARA CC Weapon (-3). MOV and PH have no printed values.

rules.name: Data Console
paragraphs: One Data Console at the center of the Server Room holds exactly one Data Pack. Represent it with a Console A Token or scenery of matching diameter (ITS 17 EN p. 48 / ES p. 67). ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 specifies 40 mm for the Console Token.

rules.name: Extract Data Pack (Attacker Only)

requirements: Only an Attacker Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Data Console may declare Extract Data Pack.
effects: Make a Normal WIP-6 Roll to Extract a Data Pack, placing a Token beside the successful Trooper. If the Data Console has been Unlocked, use a Normal WIP Roll without the -6 MOD. Failed attempts may be repeated by spending another Short Skill.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 EN pp. 48–49 and ES p. 67: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Both originals impose WIP-6 before unlocking the Data Console and unmodified WIP after unlocking; failed attempts are repeatable.

paragraphs: Only an Attacker Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Data Console may declare the Attack, Scenario Short Skill Extract Data Pack.

Perform a Normal WIP-6 Roll to Extract the Data Pack, placing a Data Pack Token beside the successful Trooper. If the Data Console has been Unlocked, the Skill uses a Normal WIP Roll without the -6 MOD. Failure may be retried by spending another Short Skill.

rules.name: Data Pack Carrier
paragraphs: The Data Pack must be represented with its Token. Its carrier must always be on the table as a Model, never in a Marker State (such as Camouflage or Holoecho).
If the carrier enters Dead State after Extracting the Data Pack, remove the Data Pack Token. The scenario's objectives refer to the Trooper that Extracted the Pack.

rules.name: Inhibitor Antenna
paragraphs: One Inhibitor Antenna stands next to an exterior Server Room corner in the Defender's table half. It uses a Transmission Antenna Token or matching-diameter scenery (ITS 17 EN p. 49 / ES p. 68), at 40 mm under the ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 Transmission Antenna chart entry.

rules.name: Use Inhibitor Antenna

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Inhibitor Antenna may declare this Skill.
effects: Choose to Unlock the Data Console (Attacker only) or to activate/deactivate the Server Room Defense System (either side). A successful Normal WIP Roll performs that action. Failed attempts may be repeated, each spending another Short Skill.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 EN pp. 49–50 and ES p. 68: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Unlock Data Console only for the Attacker; either player may activate or deactivate the Server Room Defense System.

paragraphs: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Inhibitor Antenna may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill. Choose one action: as the Attacker only, Unlock the Data Console; or as either side, activate or deactivate the Server Room Defense System.
A successful Normal WIP Roll performs the selected action. Failed attempts may be repeated, each spending another Short Skill.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for Specialist-only tasks.

rules.name: Killing
paragraphs: Troopers are considered Killed by the enemy when they enter Dead State, are in a Null State at game end, or were never deployed on the table as a Model or Marker by game end.

rules.name: INTELCOM Card (Support and Control)
paragraphs: After selecting the Classified Objective but before the game begins, each player declares whether the card will be used as Classified or INTELCOM. Both roll a die; the high roller announces first, while the mission/number on the card stays Private Information.

At the end of the final Game Round, in Initiative order, a player with at least one non-Null Trooper in the Server Room may apply the INTELCOM numeric value in Support and Control Mode to that Zone's Domination comparison.
ITS 17 EN p. 50 calls this adding the card's value to Victory Points inside a chosen ZO; ES p. 69 says Army Points (Puntos de Ejército). Preserve the source terminology difference.

condition.text: If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, the mission ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 45 and ES pp. 63–64 each print Defender Main Objectives worth 1 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 11 OP, plus one Classified OP, for a possible 12. Preserve the printed awards without silently imposing a 10-point cap.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 47 gives an [[distance:8:inch]] square Server Room while ES p. 65 says [[distance:20:cm]] square. The geometry follows English inches; these are not exact physical equivalents.
ITS 17 V0.2 ES p. 66 explicitly grants Wide Gate access regardless of Silhouette. EN p. 47 says Gates are open and describes their representation, but not that clause.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 47 counts Shasvastii-Embryo or any non-Null State in the Server Room; ES p. 66 instead specifies Normal or Unconscious.
