ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 50 applies INTELCOM numeric value to Victory Points within a ZO; ES p. 69 says Army Points (Puntos de Ejército). This is a terminology discrepancy.
ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 46 places the exclusion boundary [[distance:4:inch]] either side of center; ES p. 65 says [[distance:10:cm]]. Geometry follows English inches.

record.name: Outbreak
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Outbreak: Scan up to three Infected, Stabilize more and the Alpha Infected, CivEvac more and the Stabilized Alpha Infected, and Secure an Infected; historical scoring differs from ITS 18.

condition.text: Score 1 Objective Point for each different Infected you have Scanned by game end, to a maximum of 3. Both players may Scan the same Infected, but each player may Scan it only once.
At game end, have Stabilized more Infected than your opponent. An Infected already Stabilized by one player cannot subsequently be Stabilized by the other.
At game end, have Stabilized the Alpha Infected (ITS 17 EN p. 68 / ES p. 46). This separate 1-point objective does not exist in ITS 18.
At game end, be CivEvacing more Stabilized Infected than your opponent.
At game end, be CivEvacing the Stabilized Alpha Infected (1 Objective Point in ITS 17 EN p. 68 / ES p. 46, rather than 2 Objective Points in ITS 18).
At game end, Secure at least one Infected that you have Stabilized or are CivEvacing, with no enemy non-Null Trooper within its Zone of Control.

rules.name: Infected Placement
paragraphs: Five Infected Civilians participate; the Alpha Infected is fixed at the table center. Before the Deployment Phase, each player places two further Infected entirely within the opponent's half of the table. Their locations are chosen by players, not pre-marked on the map.

Each player-placed Infected must be at least [[distance:4:inch]] outside the enemy Deployment Zone and at least [[distance:8:inch]] from all other Infected. They cannot be placed inside or atop scenery or buildings and must be in an accessible location.

The player who kept Deployment places both of their Infected first. A Trooper may CivEvac at most one Infected at a time. Infected are represented by suitable Infinity/Infinity Bootleg Models, normally HVT or Civilian miniatures.

It is not permitted to deploy in Silhouette contact with an Infected. The English and Spanish distance conventions differ slightly: [[distance:4:inch]] / [[distance:8:inch]] versus [[distance:10:cm]] / [[distance:20:cm]].

rules.name: Corner Deployment Zones
paragraphs: Side A and Side B deploy in opposite table corners in quarter-circle Deployment Zones whose radius depends on the number of Army Points. The diagram uses top-right for Side A and bottom-left for Side B.

rules.name: Player-Placed Stabilization Zones
paragraphs: There are two Circular Template Stabilization Zones ([[distance:12:cm]] diameter each), one placed by each player. After placing the Infected and before deployment, each player places one Template totally inside their own Deployment Zone on a surface large enough for the full Template.
The player who kept Deployment places the first Stabilization Zone. Its precise position is not specified by the published map and is not invented here.

At the end of each Player Turn, an Infected being CivEvaced is Stabilized if both the Infected and their CivEvacing Trooper are totally inside a Stabilization Zone. Mark which player Stabilized the Infected with a Player A or B Token.
An Infected already Stabilized by one player cannot be Stabilized by the other, including by a Stabilization Zone.

rules.name: Stabilize Infected (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic, or Specialist Operative may declare this Skill while in Silhouette contact with an Infected or an allied Trooper CivEvacing one.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Stabilize the Infected. On success mark it with the player's Token. Failed attempts may be repeated with another Short Skill.
restrictions: An Infected already Stabilized by the opponent cannot be Stabilized again.

paragraphs: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic or Specialist Operative may use this Attack, Scenario Short Skill while in Silhouette contact with an Infected or an allied Trooper CivEvacing one.

Make a Normal WIP Roll to Stabilize an Infected. On success, mark it with the player's Token. Failed Rolls can be retried using additional Short Skills; an Infected already Stabilized by the opponent cannot be Stabilized again.

rules.name: Scan Infected (Short Skill)

requirements: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic, or Specialist Operative may Scan an Infected or Stabilized Infected in its Line of Fire and Zone of Control, whether or not the Infected is being CivEvaced.
effects: Declare an Attack, Scenario Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed attempts can be repeated with another Short Skill.
restrictions: Each player may Scan a given Infected only once. The other player may Scan that Infected separately.

paragraphs: Only a Trooper with Doctor, Paramedic or Specialist Operative may Scan an Infected or Stabilized Infected that is within the Trooper's Line of Fire and Zone of Control, regardless of whether it is being CivEvaced.

Declare an Attack, Scenario Short Skill and make a Normal WIP Roll. Failed Rolls may be retried with further Short Skills. Each player may Scan any given Infected only once; the other player can independently Scan the same Infected.

rules.name: Doctor and Paramedic Bonus
paragraphs: Troopers with Doctor or Paramedic receive +1SD to the WIP Rolls required to Stabilize, Scan or perform CivEvac on an Infected. The source does not grant this bonus to Specialist Operatives without one of those Skills.

rules.name: Secure Infected
paragraphs: At game end, an Infected that you Stabilized or that one of your Troopers is CivEvacing is Secured if its Zone of Control contains no enemy Trooper in a non-Null State.

rules.name: No HVT or Classified Deck
paragraphs: No player deploys an HVT. The HVT Model and Secure HVT rules do not apply; the Classified Deck is not used and this scenario has no Classified Objectives.

condition.text: If a player begins an Active Turn in Retreat!, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 69 requires placement at least [[distance:4:inch]] outside the enemy Deployment Zone and [[distance:8:inch]] between Infected; ES p. 47 prints [[distance:10:cm]] and [[distance:20:cm]]. Geometry uses English units; both measurements are preserved without treating them as exactly equivalent.

record.name: Akial Interference
record.summary: ITS Season 17 Akial Interference: complete Common Classified Objectives, use the central Antenna to cancel or replace public cards, and score one private Classified Objective.

condition.text: Score 1 Objective Point for each Common Classified Objective you have accomplished that has not been canceled by Akial Interference, up to 6 points.
At the end of the game, have accomplished more Classified Objectives than your opponent; only accomplishments still valid under the mission's Akial Interference rules count for the final score.

objectives.name: Complete a Classified Objective in Every Round

condition.text: Have accomplished at least one Classified Objective in each of the three Game Rounds. This is 1 Objective Point total, even if a qualifying objective was later canceled by Akial Interference.
Complete your single Private Classified Objective for 2 Objective Points. This card cannot be canceled or spent to Emit Akial Interference.

rules.name: Forces and Deployment
paragraphs: Both sides deploy at opposite table edges in the three published table-size configurations. The Deployment Zone depth is [[distance:8:inch]] at 150 Army Points and [[distance:12:inch]] at 200–400 Army Points.

It is not permitted to deploy in Silhouette contact with the central Akial Antenna or any HVT. HVT locations are selected by players under normal HVT deployment rules; no fixed HVT coordinates appear on the official maps.

rules.name: Common Classified Objectives
paragraphs: Both players share two public Common Classified Objectives in each Game Round, one initially selected from each player's Classified Deck. In the first Game Round, each player shuffles their deck in front of the opponent, draws two cards and selects one Private Classified Objective and one Common Classified Objective. Both Common cards are revealed simultaneously.

At the beginning of Rounds 2 and 3, discard current Common Classified cards that neither player accomplished, and move accomplished cards aside to preserve each player's completed record. Each player then draws two cards, chooses one as the new Common Classified Objective and discards the other.

Common Classified Objectives that normally say 'at the end of the game' or 'during the game' may be accomplished at the end of any Player Turn, but only after they have been drawn as Common cards. Both players can accomplish the same Common card in the same Round. When a deck is empty, reshuffle its discard pile.

Use Player A and Player B Tokens to distinguish which player accomplished each Common card. Only accomplished Common cards count towards the final Common Classified score, and previously accomplished cards can become invalid when canceled by Akial Interference.

rules.name: Private Classified Objective
paragraphs: Each player has one Private Classified Objective chosen from their initial draw. Its identity is Private Information. A Private Classified Objective cannot be used to Emit Akial Interference and cannot be canceled by the effect. Completing it is worth 2 Objective Points.

rules.name: Signal Redundancy
paragraphs: If, when Common Classified Objectives are revealed in any Game Round, both have the same name, the player with the first Player Turn draws another card and adds it as an extra Common Classified Objective.
Two cards with the same name, Common or Private, may both be accomplished in the same Player Turn only when they have different targets or different Troopers accomplish them.

rules.name: Multiple HVTs and Exclusions
paragraphs: Each player deploys four HVT Models following standard HVT deployment rules. Each HVT may be used for only one Classified Objective; once an HVT-targeting Objective is completed, that HVT Model is removed from the table.
Neither Secure HVT nor Secure Treasure applies (ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 33 and ES p. 60). The HVT Models themselves still deploy.

rules.name: Akial Antenna
paragraphs: One Akial Antenna stands at the center of the table (ITS 17 EN p. 33 and ES p. 60). Represent it with a Transmission Antenna Token (TRANS. ANTENNA) or a scenery piece matching the Token's diameter. The ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 13 / ES p. 14 chart fixes the Transmission Antenna Token at 40 mm.
The Akial Antenna is used by Emit Akial Interference and Filter the Signal. No deployment in Silhouette contact with the Antenna or any HVT is permitted.

rules.name: Emit Akial Interference

requirements: Only a Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna may declare this Attack, Scenario Short Skill.
The player's completed Common Classified Objective must bear one of the four symbols pictured in ITS 17 EN p. 34 / ES p. 61. Each such Common card may be chosen only once.
Each Specialist Troop may Emit Akial Interference only once per Game Round, subject to the source's unresolved wording about retrying failed WIP Rolls.
effects: Make a Normal WIP Roll to Emit Akial Interference. A failed Roll may be retried by spending another Short Skill.

On success, cancel an opponent's accomplished Common Classified Objective sharing a symbol with a Common Classified Objective previously accomplished by the player. The opponent no longer counts that card; discard it if neither player has accomplished it.
restrictions: Only accomplished Common Classified Objectives may be selected for Emission or score final Common Classified points; Private Classified Objectives are not eligible.
Each eligible accomplished Common card can be chosen only once for this Skill, and each Specialist can Emit no more than once per Game Round.
clarifications: ITS 17 EN p. 34 and ES p. 61 both say each Specialist may Emit only once per Round yet also allow repeated failed attempts; the texts do not resolve whether the limit counts attempts or successful emissions.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 V0.2 EN pp. 33–34 / ES p. 61: Short Skill with Attack and Scenario Labels; required four symbols are pictured rather than spelled out in the extracted PDF text.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna may Emit Interference if the player has accomplished a Common Classified card bearing one of the four printed symbols. Each eligible card may be chosen once.

Make a Normal WIP Roll; failed attempts may be retried with additional Short Skills. Both originals also limit each Specialist to Emitting once per Game Round without clarifying whether the limit covers failed attempts.

On success, cancel an opponent's accomplished Common Classified card sharing a printed symbol with one previously accomplished by the player. That opponent no longer counts the completion; discard the card if neither player has accomplished it.
Only accomplished Common cards score or can be selected for Emission. Private Classified cards cannot Emit or be canceled.

rules.name: Filter the Signal

requirements: A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna.
effects: Spend a Scenario Short Skill without a Roll. Choose a current Common Classified Objective card.
If either player has accomplished the chosen card, move it to the accomplished area and retain that result. Otherwise discard it. Draw a replacement card from the player's own Classified Deck.
sourceNotes: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 34 / ES p. 62: Attack, Scenario Short Skill, without a Roll.

paragraphs: Attack, Scenario Short Skill. A Specialist Troop in Silhouette contact with the Akial Antenna may Filter the Signal without making a Roll.

Choose one of the current Common Classified Objective cards. If either player has accomplished it, move the card to the accomplished area and retain that result. Otherwise, discard it. Draw one replacement card from the player's own Classified Deck.

rules.name: Specialist Troops
paragraphs: Only Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics and Troopers with [[skill:chain-of-command|Chain of Command]] or [[skill:specialist-operative|Specialist Operative]] count as Specialist Troops for this mission.
Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) Models for mission tasks reserved for Specialist Troops.

condition.text: If either player starts their Active Turn in a Retreat! situation, the game ends at the end of that Player Turn.

sourceIssues.description: ITS 17 V0.2 EN p. 34 and ES p. 61 both allow repeating failed Normal WIP Rolls to Emit Akial Interference while also restricting each Specialist to one Emission per Game Round. The sources do not explicitly distinguish attempts from successes.
